version.changelog:
- Initial public release: provides MCP server integration for the Kia Owners API to access Kia vehicle status, location, EV charge state, and remote commands using a user’s Kia Access account.
- Supports first-time MFA bootstrap and secure session management.
- Tools for reading vehicle data (status, location, charge state) and sending remote commands (lock/unlock doors, climate control, charging), with user confirmation required for all actions.
- Configurable write modes control which commands are enabled: `none`, `comfort`, or `all`.
- Emphasizes user security—no credential guessing, and confirmation before executing commands.

llm.summary: The skill controls a Kia through the user's own account and handles sensitive vehicle access, but the behavior is disclosed, scoped, and confirmation-gated.

dimensions.detail: Runtime access is proportionate to the integration: it calls Kia Owners API endpoints for the user's account and returns vehicle state/location; no unrelated local indexing, shell execution, or hidden network destination was found in the inspected runtime path.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses npx -y kiaaccess-mcp with KIA_USERNAME and KIA_PASSWORD environment variables; the inspected npm package version had no install-time scripts, though the sample command is not version-pinned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to list vehicles first, avoid guessed vehicle keys, require confirm:true for commands, distinguish dry runs from execution, and never echo passwords, session IDs, or refresh tokens.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses local persistence of a long-lived remember-me token and device ID under ~/.kiaaccess-mcp, includes a confirm-gated forget tool, and makes plaintext token export explicit and confirm-gated.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Kia Access vehicle status and commands; account credentials, vehicle location, charging, climate, and optional door lock/unlock are high-impact but directly aligned with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the MCP server your Kia account credentials and allowing confirmed commands that can affect a real vehicle. Keep KIA_WRITE_MODE at none for read-only use, use comfort only for climate and charging, and use all only if you intentionally want door lock/unlock tools available.
